# duploai_access_grant (Resource)

Lets one resource group use another resource group's AWS resources. The grantor resource group (`resource_group_id`) shares every resource of one `area` it owns — all its S3 buckets, all its ECR repositories, or its KMS key — with the grantee resource group (`grantee_resource_group_id`). The grantee may be in a different environment of the same workspace.

The grant covers resources by their platform tags, not by name: every bucket or repository in the grantor resource group is included, including ones created later, and one that is deleted simply drops out. To share a single bucket or repository, use a resource policy instead.

How it is applied in AWS: for `S3` and `Ecr`, an inline IAM policy on the grantee's role allows `s3:*` or `ecr:*` on resources tagged with the grantor's `duplocloud.ai/environment` and `duplocloud.ai/resourcegroup`. For `Kms`, a statement on the grantor's resource group KMS key lets the grantee's role encrypt, decrypt and generate data keys.

The grantee resource group must already have its IAM role (provisioned to `Complete`), and a `Kms` grant needs the grantor to have a KMS key; otherwise the grant fails. Access is one-way: create a second grant for the reverse direction.

Every argument is fixed once the grant exists: changing any of them replaces the grant (the old one is removed, then the new one is created, so the grantee briefly loses access). To avoid the gap when changing the grantee or area, set `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` and change `name` in the same apply: the new grant is created while the old one still holds its name, and names are unique within the grantor resource group. With that set, renaming alone fails, since the old grant still covers the same grantee and area.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The "shared" resource group owns S3 buckets, ECR repositories and a KMS key.
# Each grant below lets another resource group's IAM role use one of those areas.

# Same environment: the app resource group may use every S3 bucket in "shared".
resource "duploai_access_grant" "s3_to_app" {
  workspace_id              = "<workspace-id>"
  name                      = "shared-s3-to-app"
  environment_id            = "<shared-environment-id>"
  resource_group_id         = "<shared-resource-group-id>" # grantor: owns the buckets
  grantee_resource_group_id = "<app-resource-group-id>"    # grantee: gets access
  area                      = "S3"
}

# Cross environment: a resource group in another environment of the same
# workspace may pull every ECR image in "shared".
resource "duploai_access_grant" "ecr_to_prod" {
  workspace_id              = "<workspace-id>"
  name                      = "shared-ecr-to-prod"
  environment_id            = "<shared-environment-id>"
  resource_group_id         = "<shared-resource-group-id>"
  grantee_resource_group_id = "<prod-resource-group-id>" # in a different environment
  area                      = "Ecr"

  # Changing the grantee or area replaces the grant. Create the new one first so
  # the grantee keeps access during the switch, and give it a new name, since the
  # old grant holds this one until it is removed. With this set, renaming alone
  # fails, since the old grant still covers the same grantee and area.
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

# KMS: the app resource group may encrypt and decrypt with "shared"'s key,
# e.g. to read objects in its KMS-encrypted buckets.
resource "duploai_access_grant" "kms_to_app" {
  workspace_id              = "<workspace-id>"
  name                      = "shared-kms-to-app"
  environment_id            = "<shared-environment-id>"
  resource_group_id         = "<shared-resource-group-id>"
  grantee_resource_group_id = "<app-resource-group-id>"
  area                      = "Kms"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `area` (String) What is shared: `S3` (all the grantor's S3 buckets), `Ecr` (all its ECR repositories) or `Kms` (its resource group KMS key). Only one grant may exist per grantor, grantee and area.
- `environment_id` (String) ID of the environment that owns the grantor resource group.
- `grantee_resource_group_id` (String) ID of the grantee resource group: the one being given access. Any other resource group in the same workspace, in any environment. Must differ from `resource_group_id`.
- `name` (String) Name of the grant, unique within the grantor resource group. A DNS-style label (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens). Changing it replaces the grant.
- `resource_group_id` (String) ID of the grantor resource group: the one sharing its resources.
- `workspace_id` (String) ID of the workspace that owns both resource groups (path parameter).

### Optional

- `failure_retries` (Number) Number of extra polls to tolerate a transient failure status during provisioning before treating it as terminal. Overrides the resource's default; leave unset to use it.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `access_grant_id` (String) ID of the access grant.
- `artifact_name` (String) Name of what was applied in AWS: the IAM inline policy name on the grantee's role (`S3` / `Ecr`), or the Sid of the statement on the grantor's KMS key policy (`Kms`).
- `id` (String) Composite resource identifier (workspace_id/id).
- `status` (String) Current provisioning status (`Complete` once the grant is applied in AWS).

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing access grant.
#  - WORKSPACE_ID is the unique identifier of the workspace (e.g. 69b2aa30675718845bfe87a0)
#  - ACCESS_GRANT_ID is the unique identifier of the access grant (e.g. 6a2258e94703bc957a1b824e)
terraform import duploai_access_grant.s3_to_app WORKSPACE_ID/ACCESS_GRANT_ID
# Example:
# terraform import duploai_access_grant.s3_to_app 69b2aa30675718845bfe87a0/6a2258e94703bc957a1b824e
```
